ANSWER: In the combined logistic regression of treatment response (PR vs PD+SD) on BMI + Age + Gender, the Wald p-value for Age is p = 0.0025 (2.50e-03). Age was a significant negative predictor: OR = 0.924 per year (95% CI 0.877–0.972), i.e., each additional year of age is associated with ~7.6% lower odds of achieving a partial response.

1) MODEL & N
- Formula: logit P(PR) = β0 + β_BMI·BMI + β_Age·Age + β_Male·Male (statsmodels Logit, MLE, Newton–Raphson).
- n = 80 (asserted in script). Rows dropped: 40 fully-blank spacer rows + 1 stray row (Excel row 121) whose only non-empty cell was a single space ' ' in the Age column. No other rows dropped; no imputation; no other missingness in Efficacy/BMI/Age/Gender.
- Outcome: y=1 Efficacy=='PR' (n=41) vs y=0 {PD (22), SD (17)} = 39. Gender×outcome cells all ≥15 (Female 15/16, Male 24/25).

2) FULL COEFFICIENT TABLE (combined model, n=80, log-likelihood −48.5786)
term   coef       SE        z        p(Wald)   95% CI (coef)         OR [95% CI]
const  1.53129    2.77553   0.552    0.5811     [−3.909, 6.971]      —
BMI    0.16212    0.10883   1.490    0.1363     [−0.0512, 0.3754]    1.176 [0.950, 1.456]
Age   −0.0795085  0.0262977 −3.0234  0.002500   [−0.13105, −0.02797] 0.9236 [0.8772, 0.9724]
Male  −0.61320    0.54713   −1.121   0.2624     [−1.6856, 0.4591]    0.542 [0.185, 1.583]
(ref = Female; LLR p vs intercept-only = 0.00335)

3) HEADLINE AGE STATISTIC
- Wald p for Age = 0.002500 = 2.500e-03 (z = −3.023, β = −0.07951, SE = 0.02630; check: z = β/SE = −3.023 ✓).
- OR per year = 0.9236 (95% CI 0.8772–0.9724).

4) LRT SENSITIVITY (full vs drop-Age, same 80 rows)
- LRT χ²(1) = 10.518, p = 0.001182 = 1.182e-03. Wald (0.0025) and LRT (0.0012) AGREE on significance at α = 0.05 (LRT somewhat smaller, as typical).

5) IDENTIFIABILITY DIAGNOSTICS — no separation, MLE reported alone (no Firth needed)
- Converged = True in 5 Newton iterations.
- max |β| = 1.531 (flag threshold 15); max SE = 2.776 (intercept only; Age SE 0.026 — far below Hauck–Donner flag threshold of 5).
- Fitted probabilities 0.1195–0.9031 (nowhere near 0/1).
- Exact complete-separation LP test (feasibility of a signed separating hyperplane via linprog): infeasible → no complete separation; quasi-separation indicators all clear.

6) CONTEXT CHECKS (labeled as context, not the requested statistic)
- (a) Univariable logit PR ~ Age: Wald p = 0.002083 (2.083e-03), OR/yr = 0.9278 — consistent with the adjusted effect.
- (b) Age by outcome: PR mean 54.90 (SD 9.96, n=41) vs PD+SD mean 62.36 (SD 9.68, n=39) — younger patients more likely to achieve PR.

7) REPRODUCIBILITY
- Executed script: analysis_logit_age.py (workspace root). Reads data/data.xlsx Sheet1, asserts n==80, prints the full coefficient table, headline Age Wald p-value, LRT, diagnostics, and context checks. Rerun twice with identical output (deterministic; no stochastic steps).

Caveats: single cross-sectional dataset (n=80); the headline is the statsmodels MLE Wald p-value per your specification (R's default LRT would give 0.0012 — same conclusion); Groups/ECOG-PS excluded because they perfectly encode the outcome.
